title: Ratios: Simplifying, Sharing and Scaling
seo_title: Year 7 Ratio Worksheets: Simplifying Ratios, Sharing in a Ratio, Map Scales and Recipes (Free, Answer Key)
standard_text: recognise, represent and solve problems involving ratios
meta_desc: Free Year 7 maths worksheets on ratios for the Australian Curriculum (AC9M7N08): simplify ratios, share amounts in a ratio, use one known part, link ratios and fractions, recipes and map scales. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: To share in a ratio: add the parts, find one part, then multiply.
key_sub: Simplify a ratio by dividing every part by the same number. Make the units the same first.
body_html:
How it works

A ratio compares parts: 2 : 3 means for every 2 of one thing there are 3 of the other. Simplify a ratio like a fraction, by dividing every part by the same number. Use the same units first.

To share in a ratio: add the parts, find the value of one part, then multiply.

Example

Share $45 in the ratio 2 : 3.

2 + 3 = 5 parts.

1 part = $45 ÷ 5 = $9.

2 × $9 = $18 and 3 × $9 = $27.

Answer: $18 and $27

Example

Simplify 50 cm : 2 m.

2 m = 200 cm.

50 : 200 = 1 : 4.

Answer: 1 : 4

Example

The ratio of boys to girls is 3 : 4. There are 12 boys. How many girls?

3 parts = 12, so 1 part = 4.

Girls = 4 × 4 = 16.

Answer: 16

Common mistakes

  • Dividing by the number of people instead of the number of parts: $45 in the ratio 2 : 3 is not $22.50 each.
  • Writing 2 : 3 as the fraction 2/3. Red is 2/5 of the total, because there are 5 parts.
  • Simplifying without changing units: 50 cm : 2 m is not 25 : 1.
  • Adding instead of multiplying in recipes: for 6 people instead of 4, multiply by 1.5.

faq.q: How do I share an amount in a ratio?
faq.a: Add the numbers in the ratio to get the total parts. Divide the amount by the total parts to find one part, then multiply by each number in the ratio.

faq.q: How do ratios relate to fractions?
faq.a: In the ratio 2 : 3 there are 5 parts, so the first share is 2/5 of the total and the second is 3/5.

faq.q: How do I simplify a ratio with units?
faq.a: Change both quantities into the same unit, then divide by the highest common factor. 50 cm : 2 m = 50 : 200 = 1 : 4.

faq.q: What does a map scale of 1 : 25 000 mean?
faq.a: 1 cm on the map is 25 000 cm (250 m) in real life.

sets.title: Using one part of a ratio

items.q: The ratio of cats to dogs is 9 : 4. There are 10 more cats than dogs. How many animals are there altogether?
items.e: The difference is 9 − 4 = 5 parts = 10, so 1 part = 2. Total = 13 parts = 26.

items.q: The ratio of boys to girls is 4 : 3. There are 56 students altogether. How many girls are there?

The ratio of adults to children is 7 : 1. There are 21 adults. How many children are there?
items.e: 21 adults is 7 parts, so 1 part = 3. Children: 1 × 3 = 3.
